decisive_items: Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Progression from discrete right papillary edema to severe optic nerve atrophy
response.rationale: Unilateral optic nerve dysfunction with papillitis, retinal vascular leakage, and subsequent optic atrophy occurs in a patient with confirmed acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. R5 best combines the documented viral exposure/positive PCR with the optic neuritis findings, while alternatives are either too broad or too anatomically limited.

rejected.why: Captures optic neuritis but does not include the supported SARS-CoV-2 association.
Only explains the systemic viral infection, not the optic nerve/inflammatory eye syndrome.
Accounts for some intraocular inflammation but misses the dominant optic neuropathy and etiology.
Viral optic neuritis is less specific and omits the documented SARS-CoV-2 basis.
Viral retinitis is not well supported; findings favor optic neuritis with retinal vascular inflammation rather than necrotizing retinitis.
Retinal vasculitis is a component of the presentation, not the complete diagnosis.
Post-infectious timing is not clearly established because symptoms occurred during acute COVID-19; SARS-CoV-2-associated optic neuritis is more precise.
